name: Word Gets Round
tagline: Nobody near you pays extra for not knowing.
epigraph: Limes are packed by size, a bartender said. Odd ones go cheap. Measures don't mind.
glassware: highball glass (about 350 ml), filled with crushed ice

names_note: **Word Gets Round**, the room's pick (all three, r5 vote): the person's gift, passing on what they know, with Heugel's "I've told everyone" as an echo, never quoted. Also considered: *Worth Knowing* (Wren's working title; "Worth" leads *Worth the Trip*), *In the Know* (leans on *Where You Stand*'s tagline), *Odd Sizes* (about the case more than the person), *Worth Asking*.
open_items: **The plan's row was Open with two candidates;** the room kept A's PUNCH page (2014 lime crisis) but re-centred it on Bobby Heugel's packer's cases rather than the lemon as stand-in. B (Duffy's Herald Punch) is out: Duffy is now Ruler's Legend.

**Wren's story test point 5 fails to the letter** (C5): both library mentions show Heugel already an owner of many bars. Wren waived it: being the owner and still giving the trade's trick away carries the position. That is our reading, not his motive.

**Size isn't quality** (C6): no page says odd-sized limes are as good as sorted ones; the epigraph attributes the packing to "a bartender said" (E1). The key-lime yield conflict (C1) stays out. Anvil's opening year and whether Heugel still runs it are not on any page read (C3).

**No Matrix spark:** the bourbon Rickey has no sugar; what makes it interesting is the guest's own call between lime and lemon (*Codex* p. 115) and the measure that makes the fruit's size not matter. Wren ruled it not too plain for this person. Balance: highball, 13.6% / 0.15 g / 0.545%, in range through 45 ml of melt.
**The sibling Scoundrel took the Daiquiri slot** (a French 75 over ice), so this room kept to the plan's Highball (Wren: no fifth Daiquiri).
